_readme: Subtitle cues for both promo videos. Times are seconds on the landscape video timeline (the clock of audio/voiceover.wav). The landscape video shows every cue; the TikTok cut maps them through its segments (tiktok/cut.json) and drops cues that fall outside. Words come from tiktok/audio/whisper-dtw.json (node tiktok/build.mjs --words). The text of each cue is in l10n/<lang>.json under 'subs'.

cues.en: You know the feeling.
You read your notes, and your eyes drift down,
away from the people you're talking to.
Meet NotchPrompter.
Your script sits right under the camera,
so you keep eye contact the whole time.
It follows your voice, in any language.
And when you pause, it waits for you.
Go off script, and it keeps up.
NotchPrompter jumps right past it.
See? It jumped ahead with me.
Prefer a steady pace?
Just press play.
Write your script in the built-in editor,
and record yourself with one click.
It all runs locally on your Mac,
and the prompter stays hidden
when you share your screen.
NotchPrompter.
Look people in the eye.
Now on the Mac App Store.
